findings.detail: The long discusses the linked archive’s reliability and tells readers to check the market details against Reuters before drawing stronger conclusions. That source-audit instruction is not part of the account of the post and market movement.

Both medium and long copy the title and supplied synopsis almost verbatim. The long carries over an ellipsis placeholder and generic “This entry is cataloged” rationale, adding no contextual explanation of the reported layoffs.

The long ends by saying it avoids “the title’s implication of a concluded criminal finding,” although the title concerns detention centers and Russian-linked property rather than a criminal finding. This is irrelevant editor-facing framing and mischaracterizes the title.
The long begins by repeating the medium’s first two sentences nearly verbatim and adds no new operation-specific facts.

The remainder discusses what the source’s conclusions should not be treated as, the missing authorization record and what interpretation requires. It reads as an audit note, not a fuller account of the strike and capture announcement.

The long repeats the medium’s date, dismissal, acting successor and Truth Social quotation nearly verbatim. The rest mainly lists circumstances, response and consequences absent from the supplied account, without adding concrete details.
The long closes by saying what further sourcing would be required for subsequent developments. That is a source-gap note rather than additional context about the personnel change.
